note: Written before implementing the shipped detector, as the brief requires. Each entry names the exact bands, the physical signature, the reason it is not a relabel of the existing catalogue, and how it differs from everything already built. 'priority' is expected metric improvement per unit of implementation cost on a 1-5 scale (5 = best). 'status' records what measurement did to the entry: a hypothesis that was tested and rejected is more valuable than one that was never tested, so rejections stay in the table with their numbers.

hypotheses.name: H1 - topographic-edge carrier with cross-gradient confounder gating
hypotheses.signature: Multi-scale gradient/curvature ridge response of the detrended-elevation slope, multiplied by local orientation coherence and then by a gate built from the horizontal-gradient cross products of the independent geophysical layers.
hypotheses.novelty: The catalogue is a fault-trace map. Faults are expressed topographically as aligned linear slope breaks; the public catalogue does not include every such ridge in the region, because it was compiled from published mapping rather than from a systematic slope-break search. The independent layers are used only to reject ridges that no gravity or magnetic structure supports - the opposite of using them as the score, which the controls show carries no information.
hypotheses.cost: low - uses only competition bands, one 2 s Gaussian pyramid and two smoothed cross products
hypotheses.result: screen collared 0.1074 at N=40,000/sep 3, leave-one-fold-out 0.1074 vs best single-layer baseline 0.0991; the same construction without the gate (topo_ms_coh1, coherence only) scores 0.1004, so the gate is worth +0.0070.

hypotheses.name: H2 - pure gravity x magnetics cross-gradient as the score
hypotheses.layers: 13 iso_grav_anom and 2 rtp (data-domain cross product, ASEG 2012 construction)
hypotheses.signature: Magnitude-weighted alignment of the two horizontal-gradient vectors; the cross product is zero where the fields share a strike, non-zero at unmapped structural breaks.
hypotheses.novelty: The brief's own headline construction, and grep shows no sibling repository in this cohort has implemented a cross-gradient at all, so it cannot be a relabel of what those artifacts do either.
hypotheses.cost: low - the operator is ~40 lines and needs no new data
hypotheses.result: cg_gxm 0.0715 collared sits inside the no-information control band (random 0.0718, uniform lattice 0.0693); alignment-only variants are worse (0.0357 in the earlier probe). The measured cause is integral scale: both fields have along-axis autocorrelation length 2.7-8.1 km, so their 100 m gradients are interpolation texture (see field_screen.json and native_resolution.json).

hypotheses.name: H3 - resume the cross-gradient at the fields' own scale
hypotheses.layers: 13 iso_grav_anom, 2 rtp, 12 det_elev upsampled to 1-3 km before differentiation
hypotheses.signature: Same coupling operator, but the gradients are taken at the fields' integral scale so they describe real structural gradients rather than interpolation noise; the coupling mask is then relaxed back to 100 m as a confidence layer.
hypotheses.novelty: Distinguishes 'the coupling is wrong' from 'the coupling was measured at the wrong scale', which is the actual failure mode established for H2. The mask is a truth-free structural prior, so it cannot be a relabel.
hypotheses.cost: low - smoothing pyramids already exist in screen_util
hypotheses.status: tested in the multi-scale form, no gain
hypotheses.result: the multi-scale variants triple_s1 / triple_s4 score 0.0859 and 0.0846 collared, below the topographic carrier with the same operator (0.1074) and below the plain single-layer baseline 0.0991. Coarse coupling does describe real structure, but a 300 m scoring kernel cannot exploit a structure resolved at 1-3 km.

hypotheses.name: H4 - scarplet / ridge-perpendicular chains from 1 m lidar elevation
hypotheses.layers: external: USGS 3DEP best-available DEM (1 m) over the region; 19 det_elev_slope as the low-resolution prior
hypotheses.signature: Tectonic geomorphology: fault scarps are metre-scale slope breaks whose strike is far more continuous than anything the 100 m detrended elevation can show. Detect scarplets, link them into chains, emit chain pixels.
hypotheses.novelty: A fault that is missing from the published catalogue but has a fresh scarp would appear only in lidar. Nothing in this repository or in the sibling artifacts reviewed uses sub-100 m elevation.
hypotheses.cost: high - ~100 MB tiles x the region, mosaicking, and the 1 m detrending is a separate pipeline
hypotheses.result: named source: USGS 3DEP staged products, https://prd-tnm.s3.amazonaws.com/ (free, public domain, official). Not reachable from this environment: the endpoint returns HTTP 000 through the available transport, and the region is terabytes at 1 m. The competition grid is 100 m, so the whole advantage rests on the DEM being genuinely fresher than band 19 - testable only with the data in hand.

hypotheses.name: H5 - valley-axis chains in the detrended elevation
hypotheses.layers: 12 det_elev, 19 det_elev_slope, gated by 13 iso_grav_anom and 2 rtp
hypotheses.signature: Fault-controlled drainage: alluvial valleys in the Great Basin are frequently fault-bounded on one side, so valley axes and their abrupt margins trace structures that ridge detection misses because the topographic expression is a trough, not a ridge.
hypotheses.novelty: A different edge polarisation from H1 (valley margin instead of ridge crest). The catalogue is biased toward mapped surface traces; basin-margin faults are systematically under-mapped in the Great Basin because they are buried at the range front.
hypotheses.cost: medium - skeletonise the smoothed detrended elevation, keep the margins, chain them
hypotheses.status: proposed, not yet validated on holdout
hypotheses.result: not measured; the brief's rule forbids spending a submission slot before the holdout gate is cleared, so this stays a proposal.
